ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object with mass $m=2\mathrm{kg}$ is initially at rest on a horizontal ground. A force $F$ of magnitude 10N is applied at an angle of $37^{\circ}$ below the horizontal, causing the object to move a distance $s=5\mathrm{m}$ on the ground. After the force is removed, the object slides a certain distance before coming to rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the ground is $\mu=0.25$, $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. What is the work done by the thrust $F$ on the object?
2. What is the speed of the object when the thrust $F$ is removed?
3. What is the work done by friction on the object throughout the process?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a rectangular block is placed on rough horizontal ground; the arrow of force F points toward the block along an oblique line, with direction to the right and downward, making 37° with the horizontal line, and the displacement of the block is along the direction of the horizontal ground. Gravity and the supporting force are both vertical, and the displacement is horizontal. Reasoning: During the 5 m stage when it is being pushed, the work done by the pushing force on the horizontal displacement only takes the horizontal component, so W_F = F s cos37° = 10 × 5 × 0.8 = 40 J. Since the pushing force has a downward vertical component, the supporting force increases to N = mg + F sin37° = 2×10 + 10×0.6 = 26 N, therefore the kinetic friction force in this stage is f = μN = 0.25×26 = 6.5 N, and the work done by friction is W_fr1 = -f s = -6.5×5 = -32.5 J. Apply the work-energy theorem to the pushed stage: ΔK = W_F + W_fr1 = 40 - 32.5 = 7.5 J. The block is initially at rest, so (1/2)mv^2 = 7.5; substituting m=2 kg gives v^2=7.5, therefore v = sqrt(7.5) m/s. For the entire process from rest to final rest, the total change in kinetic energy is 0; gravity and the supporting force do no work, and the only nonzero work is the work of the pushing force and the work of friction over the whole process, so W_F + W_fr,total = 0, hence W_fr,total = -40 J.
